audience.programmeDescription: International Business Administration studies how organisations operate across borders and respond to economic, social and environmental change. It combines management, marketing, finance and organisational research with responsible enterprise.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The published curriculum allocates 180 EC, but its thesis-entry rules disagree about the required credits and earlier methods courses. Relevant UCR programmes have been assessed provisionally. A final comparison is withheld until the applicable entry rule can be established.

curriculum.limitation: The allocation is 150 EC of required study and 30 EC of open study. It is not yet a fully verified degree pathway. The adopted regulations require 90 programme EC and older named methods courses for thesis entry; the current thesis description instead requires 102 EC and names Academic Skills, Quantitative Methods 1 and Sustainable Entrepreneurship. Their application to the renewed curriculum needs clarification.

componentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 12-EC individual thesis. The regulations and current course entry specify different thresholds and prerequisites; entry remains unverified.
componentNotes.y3-flex: 30 EC of open study. An optional 18-EC minor, approved exchange or permitted 6-, 12- or 24-EC internship may fit within this space; approval and non-overlap rules apply.
componentNotes.y1-academic: Required 6-EC course, with a linked first-year academic English assessment; no additional credits.
componentNotes.y2-design: Required 6-EC course. Seminars are mandatory and must be completed for examination entry.
componentNotes.y3-systems: Required 6-EC course. Working-group participation and an assignment are examination-entry requirements.
